role: contribution toward v3, not a review of v2
reviewStatus: AUTHORED SOLO. Not reviewed. Reviewer B authored retention-tiers.v2 and also reviewed it; that is the same author/reviewer conflict Agent 3 is disqualified for elsewhere. Noted neutrally — B's findings are strong — but v3 should be reviewed by someone who did not write v2 or this.

confirms.B-RTV2-01: VERIFIED against the artifact. retention-tiers.v2's entire proof schema is `FindingProof`, whose rule reads 'Every finding at T1+ carries exactly one sealed proof.' There is no obligation attached to an evaluation, no no-match proof, and no verdict proof. A Run with zero findings therefore carries zero proof. This is the most consequential finding raised in this exercise so far.

theCoreProblem.statement: The retention model proves FINDINGS. The claim the product actually gates on is the VERDICT — and in CI the verdict that matters most is PASS.
theCoreProblem.why: A passing Run asserts a universal negative: 'nothing in this scope violates these rules.' That is the strongest claim the system makes and the one with the most consequence — it merges code. Under v2 it is the only claim with no evidence behind it at all.
theCoreProblem.errorClass: Third instance in this exercise of designing around the VISIBLE ARTIFACT rather than the LOAD-BEARING CLAIM. The threat model defended the platform rather than the user; the migration framing optimised porting rather than merit; this proves findings rather than the verdict. In each case the thing that was easy to see displaced the thing that mattered.
theCoreProblem.consequenceForTiers: T1 was defined as 'the spans each finding cited'. For a passing Run that set is empty, so T1 collapses into T0 exactly when the strongest claim is being made. The ladder is not merely too thin for relationship findings (A1-RT-01 / B-RT-01) — it is absent for clean runs.

reframe1_unitOfProof.was: A proof attaches to a finding.
reframe1_unitOfProof.shouldBe: A proof attaches to an EVALUATION. Every rule evaluation yields a proof of its outcome, whether that outcome is a match or a no-match.
consequences: A passing Run carries one proof per evaluation, not zero.
Baseline comparison, waiver application, and policy evaluation are themselves evaluations and acquire proof obligations — closing the rest of B-RTV2-01.
'No findings' becomes checkable rather than asserted.

reframe2_theNegativeIsTheHardOne.insight: Proving a match needs a witness. Proving a NO-MATCH needs a completeness claim: that the subject set examined was the right one and was examined entirely.

requires.why: so both membership and NON-membership are checkable — otherwise 'we found nothing' cannot be distinguished from 'we looked at nothing'
rule version plus resolved parameters; a no-match is only meaningful relative to what was asked
a no-match over insufficient facts is not a no-match; it is an unavailable result wearing one

reframe2_theNegativeIsTheHardOne.invertsTheEconomics: A passing Run's proof is LARGER and more important than a failing Run's. The v1/v2 ladder assumed the opposite — that you retain what a finding cited, so more findings means more retention. The real relationship is the reverse, and every size estimate in v1 and v2 inherits the wrong assumption.

reframe3_tierByRecomputability.problemWithBothPriorLadders: v1 and v2 both tier by CONTENT TYPE — how much source do we keep. That framing forces a direct trade between explainability and privacy, which is why V10 appeared as a contradiction at all.
reframe3_tierByRecomputability.betterAxis: Tier by RECOMPUTABILITY: what can be regenerated from what is retained, versus what is irreducible.

structure.retain: fact partition + coverage manifests + subject-set commitments + plan and rule identities
structure.property: RECOMPUTABLE — proofs regenerate deterministically from these
structure.privacy: facts are already a lossy structural projection; identifiers may still be personal data (threat-model U3) but bytes are not present

structure.property: proofs are generated ON DEMAND, not stored
structure.note: storage cost of proofs drops to zero; the cost moves to recomputation, which is bounded because the facts are already there

structure.property: IRREDUCIBLE — needed only to show a human the actual line, because fact extraction is lossy
structure.privacy: the only tier that stores user content, so it is the only one that needs a retention clock

whyThisIsBetter: It dissolves V10 rather than trading it off: explainability comes from recomputation over retained facts, and privacy comes from not retaining bytes. Both hold simultaneously.
It makes the passing-Run proof affordable — commitments are small even when the subject set is large.
It puts the retention clock on exactly one thing (source bytes) instead of on the whole evidence model.
It matches a property the architecture already sealed: facts are content-addressed and derivation is deterministic. If both hold, proofs ARE recomputable and storing them is redundant.
whatItCosts: Recomputation requires the fact partition to survive, so fact retention becomes the load-bearing durability decision rather than source retention.
It only works while the producing toolchain and rule versions remain available — proof regeneration inherits the reproducibility problem B-RTV2-08 already raises against T2.
A user who purges facts loses explainability even though no source was ever stored. That trade must be stated, not discovered.

openQuestionsThisRaises.q: Is a subject-set commitment over a large repository actually small? A set commitment is small; producing it requires enumerating the set, which is the cost the architecture already pays during planning. Needs measurement, not assertion.

If proofs are recomputed rather than stored, what does a Run's EvidenceDigest cover — the proofs, or the inputs sufficient to regenerate them? The latter seems right and changes the digest definition.

Does recomputation-based explainability satisfy an auditor who wants evidence frozen at the time of the decision? Possibly not, which may be the honest case for an explicit attestation mode rather than a general tier.

B-RTV2-07's missing proof shapes — aggregate/set, metric/derivation, policy/baseline, external-observation — need shapes under this reframe too. Recomputability may simplify them: a metric proof becomes 'the inputs and the function', not a stored number.

sealedPropertiesCovered.property: required partial coverage cannot yield pass
sealedPropertiesCovered.relevance: a no-match proof must carry coverage sufficiency, or an unavailable result can masquerade as a clean pass

sealedPropertiesCovered.property: determinism is conditional on exact Coverage
sealedPropertiesCovered.relevance: recomputability depends on it; if determinism fails, proofs cannot be regenerated and this reframe fails with it
this is the precondition that makes recomputation sound

sealedPropertiesCovered.property: minimise retention of user content (threat-model V1)
sealedPropertiesCovered.relevance: satisfied by retaining structure rather than bytes

knownLimitations: This is a reframe, not a specification. It proposes the axis for v3; it does not define proof schemas, commitment structures, or the recomputation contract.
The claim that proofs are recomputable rests on determinism and fact retention. Both are sealed properties, but neither is implemented or measured, so the reframe inherits their risk.
RQ-3 may be fatal for an attestation use case, in which case a stored-proof mode is still required and this becomes the default rather than the whole model.
Authored solo and unreviewed. The author has been wrong about this decision's center once already — recommending the T1 default that both reviewers then contradicted.
